results.market_title: Will Helen Zille be the next mayor of Johannesburg?
results.reasoning: In the November 4, 2026 Johannesburg municipal elections, DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille opened the largest-ever gap over the ANC in the city, decisively winning the plurality of seats, though well short of a majority given a highly fragmented council. As the clear front-runner and leader of the largest party, she is the natural lead candidate in ongoing coalition negotiations (as of Nov 9-16 reports), but Johannesburg's coalition politics have historically been volatile, with multiple mayors swapped in/out in prior terms due to shifting alliances among smaller parties (EFF, ActionSA, PA, FF+, Rise Mzansi, etc.). No council sitting/mayoral vote outcome had been confirmed as of the latest available reporting, leaving meaningful uncertainty despite Zille's strong positional advantage.
results.key_findings: ["DA's Helen Zille won a 'crocodile-jaw-wide' lead over ANC in Nov 4, 2026 Johannesburg election, the largest margin ever in the city (Daily Maverick)","Council is highly fragmented: several parties hold 1-5 seats each, meaning no outright majority for any party (Daily Maverick)","Zille said she would only consider an ANC-DA pact if Ramaphosa launched an inquiry into Johannesburg organised crime, indicating ongoing, unresolved coalition talks (Daily Maverick, Nov 9)","Pre-election polling (Bloomberg, Oct 4) already showed Zille as clear front-runner with 36% vs ANC's 27%, well short of 50%","No confirmed council vote/mayoral inauguration result found as of search date; coalition formation appears still in progress"]

Will the Democratic Party candidate win the 2026 NC-12 House election by 35%-40%?
results.reasoning: NC-12 is a heavily Democratic, Cook PVI D+24 Charlotte district held by longtime incumbent Alma Adams. Past actual margins in contested two-way races have run roughly 46-48 points (2024: ~47; prior map general ~46), and the 2025 GOP-controlled redistricting reportedly packed even more Democratic voters into NC-12 to protect other seats, with forecasters (e.g., Crosstab) projecting an even larger ~56-point margin for 2026. This makes a 35-40% margin plausible but likely on the low end of the realistic range, with a 40%+ margin somewhat more probable given the trend toward packing and incumbent strength.
results.key_findings: ["Ballotpedia: 2024 NC-12 general margin was Adams 74.0% vs Ali 26.0% (~48 pt margin)","Wikipedia/WFAE: New 2025 map gives NC-12 a Cook PVI of D+24, the most Democratic-favorable NC district","Ballotpedia: NC's 2025 redistricting drew several Democratic incumbents (Jackson, Manning) off their old districts, suggesting Democratic voters were further concentrated into NC-12","Crosstab.vote forecasts NC-12 as Safe Democratic with a projected D+56.3 margin for 2026","Prediction market data shows Adams at ~94% to win outright, consistent with an overwhelmingly safe seat"]

executor.read: Venue: polymarket-us. Dry run while paperTradeMode is on: every paper entry/exit of the main lane is queued as an intent and consumed on the next 5-minute cron; each is routed to the Polymarket US moneyline (league -> game -> long/short side) and priced on that book with its 0.0695 x p(1-p) fee; clobRef is the same intent on the global CLOB for comparison. Nothing is placed while dry. order = the FOK limit the executor would send (YES-price convention, tick-rounded, contracts). execPriceC = volume-weighted effective price for the paper size; slippageC = cents worse than the paper price; wouldReject = live rules that would refuse it (min size, slippage cap 5c, thin book); wouldBlock = the daily risk gates. routing.unroutable = intents with no Polymarket US market (the live path skips those trades). roundTrips diff buy+sell (both fees) against the paper ledger; dryMinusPaper is how much paper overstates. Maker mode (orderMode): a BUY rests post-only at the best level on our side (good-till-date = the TTL) instead of crossing; dry fills it when the market trades through the level or a print lands there, and at the TTL takes the taker fill (fallback) or skips; takerRef on a maker fill is the FOK it would have sent at placement, so maker.savedVsTakerUsd and roundTrips.makerMinusTakerOnFilled are the maker edge on the trades that filled; maker.missed are entries that never filled. Exits stay taker. Live: only with paperTradeMode off and PMUS_KEY_ID/PMUS_SECRET_KEY set; consumes the live exec queue, FOK limit or close-position with synchronous execution, confirms fills to the auto-trader, reconciles ambiguous sends against the account position and halts itself if that fails. POST /autotrader/executor/halt is the kill switch.

xvenue.read: polyMoves = minutes where Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c; staleKalshi = of those, Kalshi's same-minute quote was still crossable after its 7.000000000000001% x p(1-p) taker fee (avgStaleEdgeC = cents of edge per share); kalshiSameMin/NextMin = Kalshi moved the same way that minute / the next; kalshiLeads = Kalshi moved first and Polymarket followed. A Kalshi lane is worth building only if staleRate x avgStaleEdgeC is meaningfully positive over many games. us* = the same for Polymarket US (taker 9.5% x p(1-p)); kUsCross = minutes where buying on one US-legal venue and selling on the other cleared both taker fees (the only fully legal arbitrage pair for a US operator). crosses = those minutes listed (newest first, with the US shares shown on the side taken; Kalshi sizes are not sampled) and whether each was still there on the next row (persisted): the Kalshi read lands a few seconds before the US read inside a minute, so a cross gone a minute later is most likely a book catching up between the two reads; one game carrying most of a sport's crosses points at a mis-mapped Kalshi leg.

usLane.read: Paper only: each event is a hypothetical taker fill on Polymarket US at the sampled quote (px, qty = shares shown at that price; one event per game minute, on the leg the US instrument quotes). tradable = the subset with at least 50 shares shown (usd = dollars on the shown size, capped at 1000 shares) in a minute where global Polymarket's mid moved >= 3c and the US quote was still crossable after the 9.5% x p(1-p) taker fee (edgeC = cents of edge at entry). marks.* = cents per share after the entry fee, marked at global Polymarket's mid 1/5/15/60 minutes later and at the end of the game (final), and at settlement (0/1); exit fees and the US spread are not charged on those. marks.x5 / marks.x15 are the round trip: closed on the Polymarket US book 5 / 15 minutes later (the bid for a buy, the ask for a sell, so the spread is paid) with the exit taker fee charged too - what a scalping lane would actually have booked. roiPct = avg mark pnl / avg entry price. noData = horizon passed with no sample. marks.kh0 / marks.kh1 are the Kalshi hedge (Oct 30 2026): the same leg sold on Kalshi at its bid (for a buy) or bought at its ask (for a sell) as a taker, priced in the event minute (kh0) or at the next sample (kh1, the honest one: the US leg first, Kalshi a minute later); the US entry fee and Kalshi's taker fee are charged and the position is then locked whatever the game does, so this is what a two-venue, US-legal lane would book per share (Kalshi sizes are not sampled; usd uses the US shown size; noData = Kalshi not quoted there). kalshiQuoted = the events with a kh1 mark, so kh1 can be read against x5 / settle on the same events (all and tradable), with the games carrying most of them (one game holding a third or more is a stale-quote artefact, not a lane). Decision rule (docs/PROFIT-AVENUES.md Part 2): after ~200 events, a Polymarket US lane is worth building only if the round trip (x5 or x15) is positive on the tradable subset with a hit rate above 50%, or settle is; a Kalshi-hedged lane only if kh1 is positive on the tradable subset at a hit rate above 50% over ~200 events with a Kalshi quote, and it beats x5; the real-money flip stays the operator's call.

scalp.read: The stale-quote scalp lane (src/scalp.js), two venues. Polymarket US (venue 'us', mode scalpMode): each minute the sampler sees global Polymarket's mid move 3c+ while the US quote has not followed and is still crossable after its taker fee, the lane takes the stale quote for up to $10 (never more than the shares shown, 50+ required) and closes on the US book 5 minutes later as a taker. Kalshi (venue 'kalshi', mode scalpKalshiMode, sports: NHL): the same minutes on Kalshi's own YES book for the leg, a stale ask bought as YES or a stale bid sold as YES (= buying NO), up to $10, closed on that book 5 minutes later; Kalshi sizes are not sampled, so dry assumes the quote holds for that size and live sends immediate-or-cancel orders that fill what is there or nothing. pnlC is cents a share after both of the venue's taker fees (Polymarket US 0.0695 x p(1-p), Kalshi 0.07 x p(1-p)), the number the paper lane's x5 mark reads for the US venue. Modes per venue: off / dry (decisions and fills at the sampled quotes, nothing sent) / live (real orders with that venue's key, only when it is on the worker: PMUS_* for Polymarket US, KALSHI_* for Kalshi). Risk: 3 open and 40 a day per venue, one stop at -$15 realized on the day across both, one scalp per game across venues, edge >= 1c; POST /xvenue/scalp/halt is the kill switch for both and the lane halts itself on an ambiguous send or an exit it cannot reconcile. byVenue splits the record. exitKind: x5 = closed at the hold on the venue's quote; late_last_quote / no_quote = no quote at the hold (dry), closed at the last quote seen or unpriced; x_live = the venue's fill (x_live_part = a partial Kalshi fill, the rest closed later); settling = the venue refused the close (market over), the position settles there and its P&L lands in the account balance, not here. The live flips are the owner's. probe (src/fill-probe.js, Nov 2 2026): every dry entry re-reads the venue's book a few seconds after the sampler's look (t0) and 10s later (t1); per venue, thereRate = the share of reads where the entry price was still quoted on our side, enoughRate = of those with sizes, the share with at least the scalp's size behind it, qtyMed = contracts left when it was there, goneAvgMoveC = how far the quote had moved against us when it was gone, avgS = seconds after the sample. This is the dry record's missing piece: whether the quote survives long enough for a live order to hit it. fresh (Nov 12 2026): until then every Polymarket US quote (sampler, probe) came off the gateway's edge cache, up to 30s old, next to a live global quote, and a dry scalp filled at the sampled quote for its whole size. Since fresh.since a dry US scalp is the live order itself matched on the venue's book read at the moment live would send it: the fill-or-kill fills only when the whole size is offered at or better than the tick-rounded limit, at the levels it takes, with the fee per level (today.drySent / dryFilled count them, as liveSent / liveFilled do for live), and the exit is close-position on the book read at the hold (x5; x5_part when the book is thin and the rest waits a minute; an empty side three minutes running is where live halts: no_quote, today.wouldHalt). fresh holds the US venue's record (all, byMode, bySport, probe) from then on and is the one to read for the live lane. Kalshi was always read live; its dry mode still fills at the sampled quote.

investigator.read: The AI investigator's settled record as bets: it backs the investigated direction when its probability is above the market's and the other side when below, a flat $100, held to settlement. core = the paper leaderboard's rule; wide = every disagreement of 5+ points. roi.recorded is at the price recorded when it looked (Gamma's displayed probability, not an offer); c1/c2/c3 pay 1/2/3 cents more per contract plus a 0.07 x p(1-p) exchange fee, which is the range a real fill on Kalshi or Polymarket US would land in. hitPct against breakEvenPct (the average price paid) is the edge in points. events = distinct events behind the bets (buckets of one event share a cluster); tEvents / tEventsC2 = mean return over its standard error with one event's bets summed first, at the recorded price and under c2: about 2 or more is evidence, under 1 is noise. byMinEdge runs the rule at each disagreement size: a real edge grows with it. concentration shows how much is a few long shots. calibration compares Brier scores (lower is better) on every scored investigation by kind. openDrift = on the open investigations, cents the market has moved toward the agent's view since it looked. Markets are global Polymarket's; a US account would trade the same question on Kalshi where it lists one.

test.rule: Bet $25 when the AI investigator's probability for a side is 20+ points above the price actually paid for it in the order book, the question settles within 72 hours, its confidence is not LOW and the market is not weather. Held to settlement. Paper only.

test.read: The pattern from the settled record, tested forward with the rule fixed in advance (version 1). Each bet is the order a live bot would send the moment the research finishes: buy up to $25 from the real asks of the side it backs, cheapest first, never above its probability minus 20 points; what is offered there is the fill (partial when the book is thin), nothing offered there is no bet (whyNot). settled: hitPct against breakEvenPct (the average price paid), and the result before fees, with Polymarket's own fee schedule and with Kalshi's 0.07 x p(1-p) (the US venue's cost: the number to read). events = distinct events behind the bets; tEvents = mean return over its standard error with one event's bets summed first (about 2 or more is evidence, under 1 is noise). fill.avgPaidOverShownC = cents paid over the price shown when the research started. atEdge = the rule at other disagreement sizes, the whole stake at the real offer. The book is global Polymarket's; Kalshi's price for the same question can differ.
